body:
`cps/services/calibre_db_lock._resolve_lock_path` falls back to the literal `/config`
(`DEFAULT_LOCK_DIR`) rather than the configured config directory, overridable only by
`CWA_METADATA_LOCK_DIR`. On any install where `/config` does not exist — every bare-metal
deployment — acquiring the lock raises `FileNotFoundError`.

Its callers (`cps/editbooks.py` do_edit_book, `cps/api/browse.py`) therefore fail there. This
was found while considering whether `cps/api/edit.py:set_cover` should take the same lock for
consistency during PR #1739: it should, but adopting it as-is would turn a working SPA cover
upload into a 500 on exactly those installs, so the call was deliberately not added and this
was filed instead.

Smallest fix: resolve the lock directory through the same config-dir SSOT the rest of the app
uses (cf. fork #1614), creating it if absent; then add the lock to `set_cover`.
title: metadata_db_write_lock hard-codes /config, so callers break on installs without it
